blocks.text: Bifurcation's paradox: the wound (no metropolis) forced residual AP onto its **actual comparative advantages** — the east coast's longest state coastline (974 km), the Krishna-Godavari delta's agri-aqua machine, mineral belts, and a demographic spread WITHOUT a single-city gravity well. The opportunity set: **port-led industrialisation** (6→10 ports; VCIC/CBIC/HBIC corridors — the only tri-corridor state), **aqua-horticulture value chains** (the processing frontier), **energy transition leadership** (solar-wind-pumped-storage-green-hydrogen — the firm-green-power play), **greenfield urbanism** (Amaravati + Vizag's metro rise — building 21st-century cities rather than retrofitting one), **institution buildout** (Schedule-13's university-hospital constellation seeding new knowledge towns — Tirupati's IIT-IISER pair, Mangalagiri's AIIMS), and the **delivery-state brand** (secretariats-DBT as governance export).

rows: Growth & income

AP's GSDP growth generally **above national average** (agri-allied led); **per-capita income crossed the national mean** in recent Socio-Economic Surveys — from a below-average start in 2014: the headline convergence fact
Structural shape
Agriculture-heavy GSVA (~1/3) with services under-weight (no metro) — the 'strong primary, missing tertiary' signature; industry ~23-25% — the corridor bet's target variable
Human development
Strong delivery metrics (PDS, health cover, DBT reach); NFHS-5 mixed — good institutional deliveries, stubborn anaemia; education transition (English-medium, Nadu-Nedu) with learning-outcome debates
Demography

TFR well below replacement (~1.5-1.7) — **AP among India's fastest-ageing states**: the coming care-economy and workforce question (the CM-level pro-natalist debate of 2024-25 is its political echo); out-migration of graduates to Hyderabad-Bengaluru-Chennai continues — the diaspora dividend-vs-drain file
Regional balance inside AP
North-coastal & Rayalaseema packages, corridor nodes (Orvakal-Kopparthi), yet coastal-core concentration persists — Sri Bagh's question in modern dress

items: **Realised**: growth convergence, aqua-horticulture leadership, EoDB brand, welfare-delivery model, institutional constellation, energy-pipeline positioning — the residual state did NOT become the basket case 2014's pessimists predicted.

**Pending**: manufacturing share, the capital's completion, fiscal repair (the debt file), tertiary-sector depth, and converting summit-MoUs to factories — the opportunity set is real but **finance-and-continuity constrained** (HCOA-070/RMA notes' themes).

**The demographic pivot**: an ageing, sub-replacement AP must shift from job-seeking youth export to **productivity + care-economy + skilled-return migration** strategies — the freshest analytical angle on this syllabus item; pair it with the delta's climate exposure (cyclones-salinity) as the two structural headwinds.
**Verdict sentence**: bifurcation forced AP from metropolis-rent to geography-work — a harder but arguably healthier development model, ten years young and capital-hungry.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — the coastal opportunity & the decade's scorecard

items: **Developmental opportunities:** the ~**975 km coastline** (second-longest), ports (Visakhapatnam + non-major), the **VCIC industrial corridor**, aquaculture/horticulture strength, and renewable-energy potential — residual AP's endowment for a fresh growth model.

**The decade's honest scorecard (2014-24):** progress on ports, some industry (Kia, Sri City), welfare-DBT delivery and human-development gains — set against fiscal stress, unfulfilled SCS, capital-city uncertainty, and pending Polavaram/river issues.
**Comparative frame:** Telangana leveraged Hyderabad's inherited base; residual AP had to build afresh — the asymmetry defines the decade.
**Way forward:** port-led, corridor-anchored, renewables-and-agri-processing growth, with fiscal consolidation and central commitments honoured.

prelimsPointers: Residual AP has the **second-longest coastline** (~975 km) among Indian states.
**VCIC (Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor)** anchors post-bifurcation industrial strategy.

AP's **TFR ~1.5-1.7** (NFHS-5: 1.7) — among the lowest; the state debates pro-natalist policy (2024-25) and repealed the two-child local-body bar.
Agriculture & allied ≈ **one-third of GSVA**; services under-weight for want of a metro — the structural signature.
**Schedule-13 institutions** (IIT/IISER Tirupati, IIM Vizag, AIIMS Mangalagiri, NIT, IIIT, CUAP) — the knowledge-town constellation.
**974-km coastline; 10-port grid; ~400+ MTPA** capacity trajectory — the port-led thesis in numbers.

sections.heading: River-water sharing after 2014 — the twin-state hydrology

blocks.text: (Fuller hydrology in MN-PIV-RMA-015 — this note carries the Act-and-dispute frame.) The Act created **KRMB & GRMB (Secs 85-87)** with an **Apex Council** (Sec 84: Union minister + both CMs), mandated **Sec 89's** project-wise KWDT-II reference, and protected ongoing projects (Schedule 11). The decade's friction file: **ad-hoc Krishna sharing (66:34 continuing)**, Telangana's fresh-tribunal demand vs AP's KWDT-II insistence, unapproved-projects exchanges (Rayalaseema Lift vs Palamuru-Rangareddy), the **2021 jurisdiction gazette** (boards' control over listed projects — implementation partial: Srisailam-Nagarjunasagar handover friction), and Godavari's calmer ledger disturbed by diversion mega-proposals (**Banakacherla** contestation 2025-era). The **Sec 90 Polavaram guarantee** (national project) meets Odisha-Chhattisgarh backwater objections in the SC — every clause a live docket.

rows: **Process without consent**

Bill passed after the **AP Assembly rejected the reference (Jan 2014)**; Lok Sabha's chaotic passage (doors-closed telecast episode, Feb 2014) — Art 3 permits it (views, not consent — *Babulal Parate*), but legitimacy ≠ legality: the standing critique. Counterpoint: Art 3's design protects national flexibility; Telangana's six-decade demand had its own democratic weight
**Asymmetric asset-liability split**

Situs-based fixed assets (Hyderabad's endowment to Telangana) vs population-based debt (58% to AP) — 'assets by location, liabilities by headcount' as the arbitrariness exhibit. Counterpoint: standard reorganisation practice; Schedule IX/X mechanisms exist (their sloth is the real grievance)
**Unnumbered promises**

Sec 46's one-year gap support, Sec 94's 'appropriate fiscal measures' & backward-area funds, capital 'assistance' — all **amount-less obligations** whose under-realisation fuelled the SCS saga (RMA-013). Counterpoint: statutes rarely fix sums; the failure is political follow-through
**Hyderabad's decade**

Common-capital revenue accruing to Telangana while AP bore transition costs; Sec 8's Governor powers barely used. Counterpoint: ten-year access + institutional continuity had value; alternatives (UT-Hyderabad) were rejected by the movement itself
**Constitutional challenge**
Writ petitions against the Act (consent, asymmetry) remain **pending in the SC a decade on** — judicial deferral itself part of the story; the Act stands operative regardless

items: **Legal position**: Art 3 jurisprudence (*Babulal Parate 1960*) requires only the state legislature's **views** — the Act is constitutionally secure; 'arbitrary' is thus a **political-equity claim**, best argued as breach of federal comity rather than of law: frame it precisely and you out-write most answers.

**Equity ledger both ways**: AP's grievances (revenue, promises, process) vs Telangana's (six decades of safeguard breaches justifying exit) — an APPSC answer can be AP-sympathetic in emphasis but must be two-sided in structure.

**Reform lessons**: (a) reorganisation via **consent-heavy process** (super-majority views, referendums debated); (b) **quantified statutory packages** with escrowed funding; (c) **standing implementation tribunal** for asset-water-employee residues (the Act's boards/committees ad-hocism cured); (d) time-capped SC adjudication of reorganisation challenges — 2014's file as federalism's curriculum.

**Closing line**: the Act divided a state in four months and has taken more than a decade to divide its consequences — speed of surgery, slowness of healing: the sentence that summarises HCOA-069→073.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — river-water sharing after 2014

items: **The twin rivers:** **Krishna** (deficit, contested — KWDT awards, AP as lower riparian) and **Godavari** (relative surplus); the Act created the **Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) & Godavari River Management Board (GRMB)** to manage shared operations.

**The disputes:** AP-Telangana contestation over projects (**Rayalaseema Lift, Pothireddypadu vs Kaleshwaram/Palamuru**), apportionment pending a fresh tribunal reference, and the 2021 notification of board jurisdictions.

**Law, equity, lesson:** inter-state water disputes (Art 262, ISWD Act) are slow and adversarial; the lesson is the need for **basin-level, depoliticised, data-driven governance** rather than project-by-project litigation.
**AP's stake:** as the lower riparian dependent on the deltas, assured Krishna water and the completion of **Polavaram** are existential.

prelimsPointers: **KRMB & GRMB** — river-management boards created under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014.
**Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** (Art 262) governs such disputes; **KWDT** awards allocate Krishna water.
mainsAngles: 'Post-bifurcation river-water sharing exposes the limits of India's inter-state water-dispute mechanism' — examine with the AP-Telangana case.

**Sec 90**: Polavaram declared a national project; Odisha-Chhattisgarh backwater objections pending in the SC.
The **AP Assembly rejected the reorganisation reference (30 Jan 2014)**; Parliament passed the Bill in **February 2014** — valid per **Babulal Parate v. Bombay (1960)** (views, not consent).
